treatment.logline: A modest Colombo tea seller measures his cramped livelihood against the restaurant he intends to build, then returns to work.

arc.beat: The working city and a carefully prepared livelihood
The cramped business becomes the measure of a larger ambition
The dream returns to daily effort

treatment.approach: Grounded Sri Lankan everyday drama: modest scale, unforced behaviour and believable early-morning daylight. No SERIES genre is supplied; the scene plays hopeful rather than ominous. Use a street-to-counter progression, then isolate Kasun only when his ambition becomes explicit. Six essential shots total 32 seconds including handles; the editor can arrive near 28 seconds without compressing L6. D03 and D04 describe later sequences, not events to import into this scene.

treatment.geography: Vehicle and Kasun remain screen-left; customer approaches from screen-right and faces left. Road lies to the right. Kasun holds the flask in his left hand once preparation concludes. Customer collects the cup with his right hand from the counter, avoiding a hand-to-hand transfer. All counter angles stay on the road-facing side of the service axis.
treatment.key_image: Kasun beside his cramped counter, flask in hand, looking out toward a larger world rather than down at his limitations.
advice: Keep L6 intact, private and unhurried.
Treat the worn fittings as part of Kasun's working frame, not a separate poverty montage.
Do not add intelligible customer dialogue: the order is conveyed with a glance and a small cup-directed gesture.
The departure and appraisal need their full 4.5-second action window.
Avoid scenic alternates and decorative inserts; these six clips constitute the intended cut.

sequences.title: A morning's work, a larger future
sequences.purpose: Establish livelihood, generosity and ambition in one continuous morning.

editor_notes: The six must clips are the intended cut, not a locked edit: roadside master for context, counter master for preparation and return, two-shot for the transaction, medium-wide for departure and appraisal, and the single for the turn and L6. The 32 seconds include handles; target an approximately 28-second scene while keeping L6 and the 4.5-second departure/appraisal intact.

Kasun starts behind the counter at frame-left; the office worker starts off to the road side at frame-right and enters at b2. Preserve the service axis and the same modest green vehicle and early wardrobe throughout.

For the cut from the two-shot to the departure master, match the cup in the worker's right hand and the flask in Kasun's left. The cup rests on the counter between their separate hand movements; do not construct a direct hand-to-hand transfer. Match Kasun's facing-away appraisal into the roadward turn, then match his roadward gaze into the return to work.

The empty cup, preparation vessel and cloth are implied practical objects; the food stays on the counter. The customer's order has no supplied wording and is conveyed by gesture, with no invented dialogue.
Silent non-dialogue source clips prevent invented speech. Build continuous morning traffic, footsteps, pour and counter sounds as post sound where needed; keep L6 quiet, intact and unobscured.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options, not intended effects here. The locked source shots are clean if post later elects to use them; do not generate these techniques in camera.

Avoid mirrors, fast finger detail, body contact, sharply featured crowds and decorative inserts. Background pedestrians remain distant and indistinct; the scripted traffic and ordinary activity remain present.

editor_notes: The six must clips are the intended cut, not a locked edit: roadside master for context, counter master for preparation and return, two-shot for the transaction, medium-wide for departure and appraisal, and the single for the turn and L6. The 32 seconds include handles; target an approximately 28-second scene while keeping L6 and the 4.5-second departure/appraisal intact.

Kasun starts behind the counter at frame-left; the office worker starts off to the road side at frame-right and enters at b2. Preserve the service axis and the same modest green vehicle and early wardrobe throughout.

For the cut from the two-shot to the departure master, match the cup in the worker's right hand and the flask in Kasun's left. The cup rests on the counter between their separate hand movements; do not construct a direct hand-to-hand transfer. Match Kasun's facing-away appraisal into the roadward turn, then match his roadward gaze into the return to work.

The empty cup, preparation vessel and cloth are implied practical objects; the food stays on the counter. The customer's order has no supplied wording and is conveyed by gesture, with no invented dialogue.
Silent non-dialogue source clips prevent invented speech. Build continuous morning traffic, footsteps, pour and counter sounds as post sound where needed; keep L6 quiet, intact and unobscured.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options, not intended effects here. The locked source shots are clean if post later elects to use them; do not generate these techniques in camera.

Avoid mirrors, fast finger detail, body contact, sharply featured crowds and decorative inserts. Background pedestrians remain distant and indistinct; the scripted traffic and ordinary activity remain present.
blend_notes: c07 — After L6 in c05, hold the silent roadward profile over the tail of Kasun's scene audio and the morning traffic; do not interrupt L6.
c08 — Cut into c04 after the worker has left and Kasun has turned inward, then return to c04; carry c04's road ambience underneath.
c09 — After c06, extend the ending with the rising wide view over c06's traffic and counter-work ambience; no dialogue.
c10 — Cut into c03 as the worker collects the cup, then return to the two-shot; carry c03's exchange and street ambience underneath.

review.why: The locked roadside wide already locates the city and vehicle together; another establishment would repeat that information.
The preparation master holds the economical work in one continuous gesture; an additional detail would interrupt its practical rhythm.
The cup insert gives the routine service tactile emphasis while preserving the counter-mediated collection.
The flask and narrow-counter insert makes the constraints of Kasun's equipment tangible during his assessment.
A close, silent profile after L6 holds Kasun's conviction without breaking up the complete line.
The gentle crane rise places his return to work within the larger street and gives the ending room to breathe.
